prd.title: Character Extraction V2: Summary-Driven Architecture
prd.target: Rebuild character extraction from scratch using summaries as foundation, replacing complex merge heuristics with profile-first approach

executive_summary: The current character extraction system (2500+ lines in consensus.py) is fundamentally flawed because it tries to solve an ambiguous semantic problem (are these two names the same person?) with rule-based heuristics. The oracle loop has been stuck at 6.7/10 for 12+ iterations because tweaks to merge logic cannot solve the architectural problem. This PRD proposes a rebuild using a 'profile-first' approach: extract the MAIN CAST as profiles (with aliases) from chapter summaries, then deterministically search the raw text for mentions. This eliminates the global merge problem and reduces code complexity by ~80%. The new system is tiered: high accuracy for main cast (10-15 characters), best-effort for supporting characters. Critical guardrails are included to avoid new failure modes: (1) no summaries↔characters dependency cycle (summaries must run without requiring v1 characters), (2) grounding gate to prevent summary hallucinations from becoming characters, and (3) first-class support for descriptive/unnamed characters (e.g., 'the creature', 'the monster'). Designed for NEW/UNPUBLISHED texts processed locally via Ollama.

current_failures.description: Extract names → merge globally → generate profiles
current_failures.root_cause: Merge decisions require understanding character identity, but identity isn't established until profiles exist
current_failures.impact: Ambiguous merge decisions cause fragmentation (5 entries for one character) or false merges

current_failures.description: _validate_merge() rejects merges AFTER union-find has already merged them
current_failures.root_cause: consensus.py lines 1571-1850 - validation runs after LLM commit
current_failures.impact: Inconsistent state, fragmented characters, wasted LLM calls
Same character may merge in one path but not another

current_failures.issue: Conservative LLM prompts cause systematic under-merging
current_failures.description: Prompts say 'false negatives are better than false positives'
Narrator detection fails → wrong plot summary → worse character extraction
current_failures.root_cause: Narrator detection runs early without main cast context

why_current_system_cannot_be_fixed: The merge problem is semantically ambiguous - no set of rules can solve it perfectly
Structure and Summaries work because they ask objective/scoped questions
Characters asks 'are these the same person?' - requires narrative understanding, not name matching
12+ oracle loop iterations have not moved score past 6.7 - architectural limit reached
key_constraints: Texts are NEW/UNPUBLISHED - not in LLM training data
Local processing required (Ollama) for security of unpublished works
Target users are audiobook narrators who need to prep without reading the book
Tiered accuracy acceptable: high for main cast, best-effort for minor characters

dependency_cycle_fix: V2 character extraction depends on chapter summaries, therefore SummaryAgent MUST NOT depend on characters.
In v2 mode the orchestrator order should be: structure → summaries → characters_v2 (then pronunciation, etc.).
Chapter summarization may optionally use character context IF available, but must function without it.
grounding_strategy: Treat chapter summaries as a candidate generator, not a source of truth.
Every main-cast character and alias MUST be grounded by raw-text mention search.
Characters/aliases with zero hits are flagged as summary-only and excluded from high-confidence main cast by default.
descriptive_characters: Unnamed characters referenced by recurring descriptive handles (e.g., 'the creature', 'the stranger') MUST be supported as main-cast entries when they are narratively central.
Descriptive handles should be treated as canonical names when no proper name exists; epithets become aliases.

features.name: Main Cast Extraction from Summaries
features.rationale: This is the core insight: extract character PROFILES from chapter summaries (which work well), not character NAMES from raw text. The LLM already identifies who matters in each chapter summary. We formalize this into a character list.
features.current_behavior: NER + LLM extract names from raw text, then complex merge logic tries to consolidate
features.proposed_behavior: Feed chapter summaries to LLM, ask for main cast profiles directly. LLM provides canonical names AND aliases together - no merge step needed. The prompt must explicitly allow unnamed/descriptive characters (e.g., 'the creature') and must forbid inventing proper names that are not supported by the summaries.

features.name: Mention Search for Main Cast
features.rationale: Once we have profiles with aliases, searching for mentions is deterministic. No ambiguity - we know 'Gatsby', 'Jay Gatsby', 'Mr. Gatsby' are the same because the LLM told us so.
features.current_behavior: Mentions found first, then try to merge - order causes ambiguity
features.proposed_behavior: Profiles first, then search for mentions matching each character's name variants

features.name: Grounding Gate (Anti-Hallucination)
features.rationale: Summary-driven main-cast extraction is high leverage but introduces a new failure mode: summary hallucinations can become hallucinated characters. We must treat summaries as a candidate generator and use the raw text as the source of truth.
features.current_behavior: Characters may be accepted based on LLM outputs even when the alleged name/handle never appears in the book text (or only appears due to substring/formatting artifacts).
features.proposed_behavior: After mention search, enforce grounding rules: (1) each main-cast character must have >=3 total exact mention hits across canonical+aliases (configurable), (2) each alias with 0 hits is removed or flagged, and (3) any character with 0 hits is excluded from high-confidence main cast by default and placed into low-confidence output with a reason.

features.name: Supporting Cast Extraction
features.rationale: Minor characters still matter for pronunciation and context, but don't need the same accuracy as main cast. Simple NER + filtering is sufficient.
features.current_behavior: All characters go through same complex merge pipeline
features.proposed_behavior: Tiered: main cast gets profile-first treatment, supporting cast gets simple NER with light filtering

features.name: Narrator Detection from Summaries

features.proposed_behavior: Narrator detected from plot_summary + chapter_summaries, matched to main_cast entry
